text: Eintracht Frankfurt did not officially appoint a manager until 1919, when the late board member Albert Sohn coached the team. The first full-time manager, Dori Kürschner, was appointed in 1921. Paul Oßwald served as manager in three stints—two before World War II and one after—and is recognized as the longest-serving manager in club history, with a single stint lasting 6 years and a total of 14 years overall. Notable trophy-winning managers include Paul Oßwald (German championship in 1958–59), Elek Schwartz (Intertoto Cup in 1966–67), Dietrich Weise (DFB-Pokal in 1973–74 and 1974–75), Friedel Rausch (UEFA Cup in 1979–80), Lothar Buchmann (DFB-Pokal in 1980–81), Karl-Heinz Feldkamp (DFB-Pokal in 1987–88), Niko Kovač (DFB-Pokal in 2017–18), and Oliver Glasner (Europa League in 2021–22). This list excludes caretaker managers and those who managed in a temporary capacity. The information is accurate as of 20 May 2025 and includes only competitive matches. Key club achievements include Bezirksliga Main-Hessen championships in 1928–29, 1929–30, 1930–31, and 1931–32; Southern German championships in 1929–30 and 1931–32; Southern German championship runners-up in 1930–31; German championship runners-up in 1931–32; Gauliga Südwest/Mainhessen runners-up in 1936–37 and champions in 1937–38; Oberliga Süd championships in 1952–53 and 1958–59; Oberliga Süd runners-up in 1953–54, 1960–61, and 1961–62; DFB-Pokal runners-up in 1963–64 and 2005–06; Intertoto Cup champions in 1966–67; Relegation/Promotion play-off winners in 1988–89, 2015–16; 2. Bundesliga champions in 1997–98; 2. Bundesliga promotions as 3rd place in 2002–03 and 2004–05; and DFB-Pokal champions in 2017–18.
